beats.care: If you live in a PG, hostel or flat, plan to store water and expect tighter use rules if the second day comes.
beats.what: PMC is considering raising Pune's water cut from 10% to 20%. That could mean supply is shut two days a week, not one.
beats.why: Dams feeding Pune are about 80% full, versus 100% this time last year. The district collector has recommended a 20% cut.

cards.body: Last year at the same time, the dams were full at 100%.
cards.caption: Pune's dam stock now

cards.body: The Thursday shutdown started this week. PMC says it will plan for eight days before deciding whether to add a second day. Areas that already get less water may get different rules from high-supply areas.
cards.title: Not final yet

opts: Dams hold less water than last year
cards.q: Why might Pune move from a 10% cut to a 20% cut?
cards.why: Dams are at about 80% versus 100% last year, and El Niño may bring weak rain.

cards.body: The commissioner says 30–40% of the city's water leaks away, so fixing leaks is also part of PMC's plan.

cards.q: Two dry days a week. Can you cope?

hook: Could Pune go *two dry days a week* instead of just Thursday?

learn.t: PMC's commissioner says about 30–40% of Pune's water is lost to leaks before it reaches homes.

sources.name: Punekar News
sources.title: Pune May Face Two Days of Water Cuts Per Week; PMC Commissioner Naval Kishore Ram Says Decision in Eight Days

tldr: PMC is weighing a 20% water cut, which could mean no tap supply two days a week instead of one.
watch: PMC Commissioner Naval Kishore Ram said on Oct 16 a decision will come within eight days.
